<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XXV.|OF THE APOSTLES.|363}}</noinclude>being terrified, ansvvered, For this time, goe thy vvay: but in time conuenient I vvil send for thee.

{{verse|chapter=24|verse=26}}† hoping also vvithal, that money vvould be giuen him of Paul, for the vvhich cause also oftentimes sending for him, he spake vvith him. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=27}}† But vvhen tvvo yeres vvere ended, Felix had a successour Portius Festus. And Felix being vvilling to shevv the Ievves a pleasure, left Paul in prison.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XXV.}}}}}}

{{c|''After tvvo yeres emprisonment the Iewes continew their sute against him, soliciting the nevv President Festus, 6 first at Hierusalem, then at Cæsarea: 9 vvhere through the Iewes partialitie he is faine to appeale vnto the Emperour: 13 and is in the meane time brought forth by Festus (giuing him good testimonie, notvvithstanding the exclamations of the Iewes against him) vnto king Agrippa and his Queene Bernice.''}} {{dropinitial|F|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial F, scrolling foliage.png|imgsize=190px|fl={{verse|chapter=25|verse=1}}}}ESTVS therfore vvhen he vvas come into the prouince, after three daies vvent vp to Hierusalem from Cæsaréa. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=2}}† And the cheefe priests, & principal men of the Iewes vvent vnto him against Paul: and they desired him, {{verse|chapter=25|verse=3}}† requesting fauour against him, that he vvould commaund him to be brought to Hierusalem, laying vvaite for to kil him in the vvay. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=4}}† But Festus ansvvered, that Paul is in Cæsaréa: and that he vvould very shortly goe thither. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=5}}† They therfore, saith he, that are of abilitie among you, going dovvne vvith me, if there be any crime in the man, let them accuse him.

{{verse|chapter=25|verse=6}}† And hauing taried among them not aboue eight or ten daies, he vvent dovvne to Cæsaréa, and the next day he sate in the iudgement seate: and he commaunded Paul to be brought. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=7}}† Vvho being brought, there stoode about him the Iewes that vvere come dovvne from Hierusalem, obiecting many and greuous {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''crimes as v. 27''.}}∷ causes vvhich, they could not proue, {{verse|chapter=25|verse=8}}† Paul making ansvver, That neither against the lavv of the Iewes, nor against the temple, nor against Cæsar haue I any thing offended. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=9}}† But Festus vvilling to shevv the Iewes a pleasure, ansvvering Paul, said, Vvilt thou goe vp to Hierusalem, and there be iudged of these things before me? {{verse|chapter=25|verse=10}}† And Paul said, At Cæsars iudgement seate doe I stand, vvhere I ought to be iudged: the Iewes I haue not hurt, as thou very<noinclude>{{rh||Zz ij|vvel}}</noinclude>
